neighbours.label: the head noun or relativizer of a technical definition ('a knot is a closed curve that...', 'a graph is a structure where...'), as against everyday 'X is a Y' descriptions
fire: In topology, a knot is a closed curve that does not intersect itself.
Formally, a graph is a structure where vertices are joined by edges.
In logic, a tautology is a formula that is true under every assignment.
A tensor is an array of components which transform under a change of basis.
In physics, a field is a quantity that has a value at every point in space.
Roughly speaking, a manifold is a space which looks flat near each point.
In set theory, a relation is a subset of pairs that satisfies a given rule.
In economics, a public good is a commodity whose use by one person does not reduce its supply.
quiet: In our garden, the shed is a wooden hut that my father built.
Honestly, my brother is a cook who works late every night.
In winter, the lake is a popular spot for families.
My car is an old model which still runs well.
In town, the bakery is a shop that opens at six.
Roughly speaking, the trip is a drive of four hours.
At school, my teacher is a woman who loves poetry.
In the village, the pub is a building whose roof leaks every spring.

notes: Probe: planar tangle 'diagram where' 0.45, vector 'quantities that' 0.31, group 0.23; 'my dog is a friendly animal that' 0.03.
